title: Fabrication and characterization of aligned carbon nanotubes/epoxy composites.
author: Diego Sadao Saito
abstract: A very new kind of high performance materials is being developed by the encounter of composite materials and nanotechnology, resulting in the so called nanostructured materials. These materials are the state of art for aerospace future applications. In this work, we dealt with fabrication and characterization of a nanostructured material made by Carbon Nanotube (CNT) and Epoxy. The main idea of the present work is to develop a method to fabricate composites with high volume fraction in CNT. Firstly, CNT/Epoxy composites were fabricated with fixed CNT volume fraction (VF), which corresponded to as-grown CNT forest VF (~1%). Several epoxies were tested as matrix and the majority led to well wet forest despite of some undesired effects arisen from fabrication method. Parametric studies, including the size of the CNT forest, were performed in order to determine which conditions would produce the least imperfections in the resultant composite. A novel fabrication method was developed to fabricate CNT/Epoxy composites with higher CNT volume fraction. This method is based on mechanical compression of CNT forest in transverse direction. The results obtained from this method were composites with the maximum VF already reported for CNT based composite fabrication using vertically aligned CNT forest. Two alternative methods based on capillarity forces induced by solvent evaporation were applied and compared to the developed mechanical method. In order to verify cristallinity in polymeric matrix, thermoplastic polymers were used to fabricate composites with CNTs. X-ray scattering analysis was applied to them and to CNT/Epoxy composites as well. Finally, samples were characterized mechanically and electrically in order to obtain the main properties of the novel material developed in this work.
